Chapter 9: Building Supportive Environments and Systems
As you start to build momentum with the slight edge, there’s a next step that can make everything feel so much easier. It’s about shaping your environment and creating simple systems that almost nudge you toward the right choices—without having to grit your teeth or rely on sheer willpower every time.
Think about willpower for a moment. Sure, it’s handy, but let’s be honest—there’s only so much of it to go around in a day. The people who consistently make good choices? Most of them have set things up so the easier path is the one they actually want to take.
Picture your environment like the wind. Sometimes, it’s pushing you forward, making progress feel effortless. Other times, it’s right in your face, and every step feels like a battle. When your surroundings are in sync with your goals, those little daily disciplines become second nature.
So, how do you build a supportive environment? Here are a few easy strategies:
First, try removing temptations. If you’re aiming to eat healthier, don’t just hide the chips—get them out of the house completely. Or, if you’re saving money, unsubscribe from those tempting shopping emails. Out of sight, out of mind really works.
Next, add some visual cues. Want to get back into running? Place your shoes right by the door so you see them every morning. Hoping to read more? Keep a book on your nightstand as a gentle reminder.
And don’t forget about automation. Set up automatic transfers to your savings account, or schedule recurring reminders on your calendar for those habits you’re building. The less you have to remember, the more likely you are to stick with it.
Now, let’s talk about systems. A system is just a routine or process that makes it easier to repeat something you want to do. For example, meal prepping on Sundays can make healthy eating almost automatic throughout the week. Or, setting a regular bedtime means you don’t have to negotiate with yourself every night.
It’s not just about the stuff around you, either. The people in your life matter, too. When you spend time with folks who share your values and goals, it’s so much easier to stay on track. Maybe that means joining a walking group, teaming up with an accountability partner, or just telling a friend about what you’re working toward.
Here’s a real-life example. Imagine someone who wants to write every day. They might set up a dedicated workspace, choose a specific writing time, and use a simple checklist to track their progress. By clearing away distractions and making writing as easy as possible, it stops being a struggle—it just becomes another part of the day.
The real aim isn’t to test how strong your willpower is. It’s to design your life so those positive choices almost happen by default. Over time, these supportive environments and systems are what keep your slight edge habits steady and strong, holding everything together.
